leeWayHeader.what: Define LeeWay's free-setup, active-service charging, ownership disclosure, and zero-mandatory-operator-cost contract.
leeWayHeader.why: Allow transparent charges for active LeeWay services without billing people for setup or non-use and without making the Creator depend on compulsory provider spending.
leeWayHeader.who: Creator, LeeWay Standards, Runtime owners, and application maintainers.
leeWayHeader.how: Require a no-cost setup path, charge only for defined active services, stop LeeWay billing when service use stops, disclose ownership per asset, and retain local/self-hosted operator paths.

requirements: A payment gate must name the specific active LeeWay service being purchased.
A payment gate must not charge for account creation, initial configuration, exported configuration, or access to the independently available backend contract.
When a customer stops using a billed LeeWay service, LeeWay recurring service billing must stop under the applicable service terms.
Provider charges selected directly by the owner must remain disclosed as provider charges, not LeeWay service charges.

ownershipDisclosure.principle: Ownership, license, hosting custody, portability, and post-service access vary by asset and service; they must be stated specifically rather than implied by a universal ownership claim.

storageAndHostingOwnership.principle: A user's files, storage selection, backup location, and provider credentials remain that user's controlled resources. LeeWay adapters configure and access them only with owner authorization.

commerceBoundary.principle: LeeWay may charge for clearly defined active product, subscription, marketplace, or managed services. Such commerce must never be recast as a mandatory payment to configure, develop, self-host, export configuration, or use the independently available backend and user-owned storage path.
commerceBoundary.requiredDisclosure: A surface presenting a payment gate must identify the product or provider being purchased, state whether a self-hosted or owner-selected alternative exists, and never claim that the core LeeWay backend is paid-only.

externalProviderBoundary.principle: External provider plans, account eligibility, device platform restrictions, and hosting outages must be disclosed accurately and must never be mislabeled as a compulsory LeeWay backend fee.
externalProviderBoundary.fallbackRule: Offer the authorized self-hosted, owner-selected, or local path when it exists; otherwise report the unavailable external boundary plainly.

operatorCostBoundary.principle: The Creator's LeeWay operation must have an authorized zero-mandatory-provider-cost deployment path. Managed hosting is optional, never the sole required runtime path.
operatorCostBoundary.requiredDisclosure: Hardware, electricity, internet access, domain registration, and optional third-party provider charges may still exist. They must be disclosed as external costs; this policy does not fabricate a claim that every physical or third-party resource is free.

runtimeAndDeviceBoundary.authorizationRule: Owner authentication, per-device consent, capability grants, Formula, Veritas, receipts, and platform permission remain required and are not monetization controls.

sourceRequirements: No developer, setup, configuration, backend-contract, or user-owned-storage path may require a mandatory LeeWay payment.
Each billed LeeWay surface must identify its active service and present the applicable non-use billing state.
Each product must disclose customer data/export ownership and post-service terms at an asset or service level.
Each backend adapter must document its self-hosted or owner-selected alternative when technically applicable.
Optional commerce gates must identify their product/provider scope and must not disable the independently available backend contract.
Core LeeWay deployments must retain a documented zero-mandatory-provider-cost path.
Runtime errors must preserve the actual external-provider or authorization boundary.
Application manifests and UI policy adapters must distinguish disabled authorization from external-provider availability.
acceptance: Each product surface is tested for free setup, active-service charging, no-use billing cessation, owner-controlled storage, and truthful commerce presentation.
Production evidence records each external provider dependency and each optional paid service separately from the free backend contract.
